experiment.title: Functional classification of 331 clinical KCNQ2 variants
experiment.shortDescription: Electrophysiologic analysis of clinical KCNQ2 variants (205 missense variants, 30 non-missense and 43 synonymous variants)
experiment.abstractText: Epilepsy is the second leading neurological disorder worldwide. Channel dysfunction caused by KCNQ2 variants leads to benign familial neonatal seizures and epileptic encephalopathy. As one of the most common epilepsy-associated genes, KCNQ2 variants explosively emerge in recent years. However, the paucity of functional interpretation on variants hinders the diagnosis and treatment of KCNQ2-related diseases. Here, we collected 331 clinically significant KCNQ2 variants: 145 from 232 epilepsy patients and other 186 missense variants from ClinVar database. To get enough negative controls, we also selected all 14 B/LB missense variants from ClinVar database and 43 synonymous variants with the minor allele frequency (MAF) greater than the incidence of KCNQ2-related disorders (0.0059%) from the gnomAD database as benign controls. All variants were performed electrophysiologic analysis and functional classification when expressed as homomeric mutant channel and as heteromeric mutant/wild type channel.
experiment.methodText: We collected information from 232 patients diagnosed with KCNQ2-related disorders. 145 KCNQ2 variants (including 115 missense variants and 30 non-missense variants) were identified by sequencing. Other 190 KCNQ2 missense variants and 43 synonymous variants from ClinVar and gnomAD database were added. In vitro functions of the total 357 variants were tested using whole-cell patch clamp recording in CHO cells. We generated functional classifications of KCNQ2 variants expressed as homomeric mutant channel and as heteromeric mutant/wild-type (WT) channel which mimicked the heterozygous state in patients. Average whole-cell currents at +40 mV or -40 mV for these variants were divided by the cell capacitances to obtain the whole-cell current density scores at +40 mV or -40 mV. Whole-cell current density amplitudes at +40 mV/-40 mV were normalized by whole-cell current of WT KCNQ2 to get the normalized current density. Conductivities (G) were calculated according to the formula: G = I/(Vm-Vrev). Voltage-dependent activation was fitted using the following Boltzmann equation: G/Gmax = 1/{1 + exp[(V1/2 − Vm)/k]}, where Gmax is the maximum conductance, V1/2 is the half-activated voltage and k is the slope factor. Shifted V1/2 = V1/2 of KCNQ2 variant - V1/2 of WT KCNQ2.

experiment.abstractText: Epilepsy is the second leading neurological disorder worldwide. Channel dysfunction caused by KCNQ2 variants leads to benign familial neonatal seizures and epileptic encephalopathy. As one of the most common epilepsy-associated genes, KCNQ2 variants explosively emerge in recent years. However, the paucity of functional interpretation on variants hinders the diagnosis and treatment of KCNQ2-related diseases. Here, we collected 331 clinically significant KCNQ2 variants: 145 from 232 epilepsy patients and other 186 missense variants from ClinVar database. To get enough negative controls, we also selected all 14 B/LB missense variants from ClinVar database and 43 synonymous variants with the minor allele frequency (MAF) greater than the incidence of KCNQ2-related disorders (0.0059%) from the gnomAD database as benign controls. All variants were performed electrophysiologic analysis and functional classification when expressed as homomeric mutant channel and as heteromeric mutant/wild type channel.
experiment.methodText: We collected information from 232 patients diagnosed with KCNQ2-related disorders. 145 KCNQ2 variants (including 115 missense variants and 30 non-missense variants) were identified by sequencing. Other 190 KCNQ2 missense variants and 43 synonymous variants from ClinVar and gnomAD database were added. In vitro functions of the total 357 variants were tested using whole-cell patch clamp recording in CHO cells. We generated functional classifications of KCNQ2 variants expressed as homomeric mutant channel and as heteromeric mutant/wild-type (WT) channel which mimicked the heterozygous state in patients. Average whole-cell currents at +40 mV or -40 mV for these variants were divided by the cell capacitances to obtain the whole-cell current density scores at +40 mV or -40 mV. Whole-cell current density amplitudes at +40 mV/-40 mV were normalized by whole-cell current of WT KCNQ2 to get the normalized current density. Conductivities (G) were calculated according to the formula: G = I/(Vm-Vrev). Voltage-dependent activation was fitted using the following Boltzmann equation: G/Gmax = 1/{1 + exp[(V1/2 − Vm)/k]}, where Gmax is the maximum conductance, V1/2 is the half-activated voltage and k is the slope factor. Shifted V1/2 = V1/2 of KCNQ2 variant - V1/2 of WT KCNQ2.
